projects.title: Real-Time Object Detection API
projects.tagline: A tested FastAPI service for a YOLO26n detector fine-tuned on African Wildlife.
projects.problem: A trained detector in a notebook is hard for anything else to use. Other services need to send an image over HTTP and get structured results back, the API must not fall over on bad input, and someone needs to know how accurate the model really is.
approach: Fine-tuned COCO-pretrained YOLO26n for 30 epochs at 640 px on the 1,052 training images of the public African Wildlife dataset (buffalo, elephant, rhino, zebra).
Reported accuracy on the 227-image test split, which was never used for training or for picking the best epoch.
Served it with FastAPI: GET /health, POST /predict (JSON boxes, classes, scores) and POST /predict/annotated (JPEG). The model loads once at startup with a warm-up inference.
Validated uploads (type, size, decodability) and returned 415 / 413 / 400 / 422 errors instead of HTTP 500.
Found and fixed an evaluation bug: an NMS time limit was silently dropping boxes on a busy GPU, so evaluate.py now disables it.
honestNotes: The GPU was shared with other jobs during benchmarking, so p95 latency is noisy (GPU client p95 397 ms).
The Dockerfile (CPU-only PyTorch, non-root user) is written but was not built on the dev machine.

projects.title: Multimodal Document RAG
projects.tagline: Question answering over scanned documents with OCR retrieval and a 4-bit Qwen2.5-VL reader.
projects.problem: Useful information sits in scanned invoices, bank statements and bills. Plain text RAG fails because there is no text layer, and after OCR the layout is easy to lose. A vision-language model reads a page image well but cannot look through hundreds of pages per question.
approach: Ingest PDFs (text layer plus a page render) and scans (RapidOCR), then split pages into 60-word chunks with a 15-word overlap.
Index every chunk with BM25 and with MiniLM embeddings in FAISS, plus a reciprocal-rank-fusion hybrid.
Qwen2.5-VL-3B (4-bit) reads the answer from the page image and the page's OCR text.
Built a seeded, privacy-safe synthetic evaluation set (45 documents, 120 questions with known answers) and measured retrieval and end-to-end accuracy.
Traced every wrong answer to a retrieval miss caused by OCR merging words, not to the reader.

metrics.label: BM25 page hit@1 on OCR'd scans
Reader accuracy when the right page was retrieved
metrics.context: every error was a retrieval miss

metrics.label: Peak VRAM
metrics.context: fits a 4 GB laptop GPU; about 3.1 s per question

honestNotes: The test set is small and templated: every question contains a unique identifier, which favours BM25. A public benchmark such as DocVQA is the next step.
The evaluation documents are synthetic and marked SAMPLE - SYNTHETIC DATA.

projects.title: RAG Retrieval Benchmark & CI Gate
projects.tagline: BM25 vs dense vs hybrid vs re-ranking on BEIR SciFact, with a CI gate for retrieval regressions.
projects.problem: Most RAG demos pick a retriever and never measure it. Without a golden set you cannot tell whether hybrid search or a re-ranker helps, what it costs in latency, or whether a small code change silently made retrieval worse.
approach: Ran four arms over the full 5,183-document SciFact corpus: BM25, dense (bge-small-en-v1.5 + FAISS), hybrid Reciprocal Rank Fusion and a cross-encoder re-ranker.
Scored all 300 test queries with nDCG@10, Recall@100 and MRR@10, and tested every arm against BM25 with a paired t-test and a Fisher randomisation test.
Tuned the RRF constant on the 809 train queries only, then froze it before touching test.
Served the arms through FastAPI GET /search and added a regression gate that exits non-zero when nDCG@10 drops more than 0.02 below the committed baseline.
Showed the gate failing on a deliberately broken branch (documents cut to 128 tokens) and documented a real regression it lets through (dropping titles).

metrics.label: Hybrid nDCG@10
metrics.context: vs 0.676 for BM25, 300 SciFact test queries

metrics.label: Significance vs BM25
metrics.context: paired t-test p = 1.7e-06; Fisher randomisation p < 1e-04

metrics.label: Regression caught by the gate
metrics.context: dense nDCG@10 drop on the 128-token truncation branch, tolerance 0.02

honestNotes: The cross-encoder re-ranker scored 0.687 nDCG@10 and did not beat hybrid on SciFact.
Hybrid vs dense alone (+0.014 nDCG@10) is not statistically significant (p = 0.19).
Latency was measured on a shared laptop GPU and varied a lot between runs.

projects.title: Self-Correcting Text-to-SQL Agent
projects.tagline: A local 1.5B model writes SQL behind a read-only safety guard, retries on errors and is ablated on Spider.
projects.problem: Small local LLMs can write SQL, but their output cannot be run as-is: they invent column names, copy identifiers from examples and will write DELETE if asked. Advice like few-shot or self-correction has to be measured, not assumed.
approach: qwen2.5-coder:1.5b through Ollama turns a question into one SELECT; a sqlglot guard and a read-only, time-limited executor run it.
On an error, empty result or guard rejection, the feedback goes back to the model for up to 2 retries.
Measured each component on a fixed, hardness-stratified 200-question Spider-dev slice with Wilson intervals and McNemar tests.

metrics.label: Best 1.5B execution accuracy
metrics.context: linking + self-correction (A1R) vs 60.5% zero-shot; +3.0 points, not significant (p = 0.070)

metrics.label: Red-team prompts that executed a write
metrics.context: guard falsely rejected 0 of 9,693 gold Spider queries

honestNotes: Few-shot examples from other databases hurt accuracy by 5 points; on this hardware model size mattered more than any prompting component.

images.alt: Execution accuracy per ablation arm with Wilson confidence intervals, and per Spider hardness level
images.caption: Execution accuracy per arm on the 200-question Spider-dev slice.

projects.title: Hinglish Sentiment Benchmark
projects.tagline: TF-IDF vs fine-tuned MuRIL vs a prompted 1.5B LLM on code-mixed tweets, served as INT8 ONNX.
projects.problem: Indian social media text often switches between Hindi (in Latin script) and English with non-standard spellings, and single-language tools handle it badly.
approach: Compared three arms on the official SemEval-2020 SentiMix test split (3,000 tweets): TF-IDF + logistic regression, MuRIL fine-tuned on a 4 GB GPU, and Qwen2.5-1.5B prompted 6-shot.
Exported the best MuRIL run to ONNX, quantized it to INT8 with outlier layers kept in FP32, and served it with FastAPI.

metrics.label: MuRIL weighted-F1
metrics.context: mean of 3 seeds on 3,000 test tweets (prompted LLM: 47.7 on a 600-tweet sample)

metrics.label: INT8 model size
metrics.context: down from 906 MB, weighted-F1 70.4, 97.3% agreement with FP32

honestNotes: The best SemEval-2020 Hinglish system scored 75.0, about 5 points above this model. Fine-tuning beat the TF-IDF baseline by only 0.9 points.

images.caption: Confusion matrices per arm. Most errors sit on the neutral class.

projects.title: Credit Risk Scoring with DuckDB and LightGBM
projects.tagline: A Home Credit default-risk pipeline: DuckDB SQL features, LightGBM, calibration, SHAP and a cost-based threshold.
projects.problem: Home Credit lends to people with little credit history. Predicting default needs the application plus history spread over 6 secondary tables with one-to-many keys.
approach: One DuckDB SQL file per table aggregates history to one feature row per applicant, with leakage checks written as tests.
Logistic regression baseline and LightGBM, isotonic calibration, SHAP explanations and a threshold chosen from an explicit cost matrix, all tracked in MLflow.
